caption: The drawing depicts two pottery vessels, one above the other, on a textured beige background that resembles a sheet from a spiral-bound sketchbook, with visible spiral holes along the left edge. Both vessels are rounded with wide, open mouths and are decorated with intricate geometric patterns. The upper vessel features angular, zigzag, and step-like designs primarily in black and brown tones, with some lighter filling; the pattern bands encircle both the main body and the neck of the vessel. The lower vessel also displays a combination of black and brown tones, but its patterns are curvilinear and angular, with a focus on bold, repetitive abstract motifs that encircle the neck and body. The vessels are shaded to suggest volume and curvature. Handwritten notes in pencil are present around each vessel, indicating information about the objects such as date, location, and material: “Pottery - Clay, Decoration, Painted” with “Zuni” specified as provenance, along with dates “October 15, 1934” and “October 14”, and references to “South West Hall Case No 1” and “Vincent Busby.”
title: Vessel
